items.title: RT by @ChrisO_wiki: EXCLUSIVE: Andy Burnham is considering requests from Saudi Arabia for a range of military support to counter attacks from the Houthis, as the UK fears a “catastrophic” economic hit from a new front in the Iran war. The Saudi asks include operational support for its military to repel the Houthis’ push along the Red Sea coast toward the Bab el-Mandeb Strait, a key trade chokepoint, and help to defend against strikes on its oil infrastructure, sources tell Bloomberg. Burnham has agreed to send British military advisers to Saudi Arabia in response to the requests, sources say. It’s unclear whether he’s willing to approve the other asks, which haven’t been disclosed by the UK government. The Foreign Office and MoD declined to answer questions. Burnham is facing one of his first major foreign policy and economic dilemmas since he became PM. Britain is determined not to get drawn into the conflict, not least because it didn’t support Trump’s war on Iran. Yet the crisis poses serious challenges ahead of next month’s budget. Burnham has been advised by his officials that if the Houthis take control of the Bab el-Mandeb Strait it will have a “catastrophic” impact on international shipping and provide another hit to the global economy through a further spike in the oil price and inflation, the sources said. The Houthi attacks have sent Brent crude toward $110 a barrel. Gilts extended a drop today as money markets added to bets on Bank of England interest rate rises off the back of inflation fears. Traders now fully price five quarter-point BoE hikes by the end of 2027, an outcome that would badly complicate the PM’s key pledge to reduce the cost-of-living. The Treasury is also worried that the recent escalation is taking place as the OBR prepares its economic and fiscal forecasts for the budget. John Healey had been hoping for a market reprieve during the assessment window. Instead it’s going further in the wrong direction and potentially leaving the chancellor with even more of a fiscal hole. Under Rishi Sunak the UK hit Houthi targets in Yemen to combat disruption in the Red Sea. Under Keir Starmer it deployed Sky Sabre air defences to help Riyadh. https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2026-09-14/burnham-mulls-saudi-support-amid-uk-fears-of-houthi-economic-hit

items.title: RT by @RALee85: A busy start to the political week here in Kyiv: Ukraine's prosecutor general, Ruslan Kravchenko, appointed by Zelenskyy last year with backing of his then-chief of staff now accused of corruption Andriy Yermak, has resigned and fled Ukraine after becoming embroiled in a corruption scandal of his own. Kravchenko's appointment was part of Zelenskyy's ultimately disastrous effort to bring Ukraine's independent anti-corruption agencies NABU and SAPO under tight presidential control through Kravchenko's oversight — a move that backfired spectacularly last summer, triggering the country's first and largest public protests since Russia's full-scale invasion. Now Kravchenko himself is facing scrutiny from those very agencies, who've charged several of his subordinates in the prosecutor general's office in an alleged fraud scheme. Before resigning and fleeing, he moved against their directors by signing off charges against them. Zelenskyy has called on parliament to swiftly approve Kravchenko's dismissal.

NABU says no suspicion has been formally served and denied Kravchenko's claims that it removed criminal cases, calling his statements public rather than procedural. Zelensky said Kravchenko has only one path left: dismissal, and urged parliament to act immediately. Kravchenko confirmed he is currently abroad on an official trip, where he says he plans to brief international partners on the anti-corruption system. Parliament is expected to vote on his resignation tomorrow. #Ukraine

items.title: “Ukraine is bracing for a brutal winter as intensified Russian attacks on the country's infrastructure and key export industries compound a deepening budget crisis, ‌Ukrainian officials said on Saturday. Economy Minister Oleksandr Kravchenko said that damage to infrastructure and fixed assets from Russian air strikes was estimated at close to $10 billion this year, while the broader economic costs of the attacks and the de facto blockage of its ports were seen at about 1.5 percentage points of gross domestic product… About $40 billion in export revenue is at risk as a result of the blockade, Kravchenko said. items.title: “It is so dangerous now in Slovyansk and Kramatorsk that police say it is time for civilians to get out. These neighbouring cities are the biggest still under full Ukrainian control in the eastern Donbas region. In the worst affected areas, forced evacuations of families with children have already begun, says Pavlo Dyachenko of Donetsk police. ‘This is the only way to save your life,’ he says, because security has deteriorated so much. ‘If you take Slovyansk, it used to be hit by glide bombs roughly once a week, but now it's almost every day…’ Over the summer, the number of civilians wounded by Russian attacks on the two cities increased from 70 in June to 212 in August, say Ukrainian police. Sixteen people died in June, 20 in July and 15 in August.” https://www.bbc.com/news/articles/cwyz89w59l3o

items.title: "Russia’s oil-processing is being degraded as sanctions prevent the refining industry from recovering from more intense and precise Ukrainian drone strikes, according to the International Energy Agency. 'It now appears likely that the persistent drone strikes and the patchwork nature of repairs are having a cumulative negative effect and degrading the refining system,' the Paris-based agency said in a monthly oil report published Friday. Ukraine has been attacking Russia’s energy infrastructure to reduce the nation’s ability to process and export crude and curtail the Kremlin’s revenues used to finance the full-scale invasion. In August, the Russian oil refineries were hit at least 22 times, the highest monthly total since the start of the war, according to a Bloomberg tally based on public statements from both nations. The IEA revised down its baseline outlook for Russian oil processing over the next 18 months to around 4 million barrels a day, down 30% from levels before the invasion of Ukraine, it said." https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2026-09-11/ukraine-strikes-degrade-russian-oil-refining-industry-iea-says

1/ EXCLUSIVE: at @RFERL we obtained photos of a Russian flotilla in Tartus port, taken early September. This is the 1st instance in months of a Russian military ship being docked there, month after the announcement that Russia’s bases in Syria would be 'transferred' to Damascus.
GeoInsider (@InsiderGeo)
UPDATE: 🇷🇺🇸🇾 After around two months of absence, Russia is back in the Mediterranean, with a Russian naval convoy now arriving at Tartus, Syria.
Our team at @SONARROW_OSINT has been tracking the convoy since August 25. The four Russian vessels have travelled from the Atlantic into the Mediterranean and across the region before reaching the Syrian coast.
The SPARTA Ro-Ro cargo ship and AKADEMIK PASHIN replenishment oiler are now docked at Tartus. The SPARTA appears to have already unloaded its cargo.
The ADMIRAL LEVCHENKO Udaloy-class destroyer and GENERAL SKOBELEV tanker are not currently inside the port. They may be operating offshore, similar to how the ADMIRAL FLOTA KASATONOV has operated around Tartus in recent months.
What exactly was delivered to Tartus remains unclear, but the return of a Russian convoy to the Syrian port after months away is significant.
So the key questions remain: What did SPARTA bring to Syria, and how long will the Russian vessels remain at Tartus?

items.title: The Russian salient north of Lyman, Donetsk region, Ukraine has collapsed. Ukrainian forces are moving into this area, conducting mopping up operations. It is only a matter of time until all Russian units in that former salient have been dislodged or neutralized. Basically the entire Russian invasion force west of the Zherebets' River in this sector is currently in utter disarray. It took Russian more than a year and countless losses to even establish that salient. The Russian propaganda announced Lyman's fall already. Seeing the collapse in a matter of weeks only paraphrases the absolute insanity of the Russia tactics to mindlessly throw in bodies with virtually zero gain and now even a territorial loss. Far worse for the Russian invasion is the setback on the operational level. Their movements have already been minuscule. Lyman is vital if Russians want to move forward. Even according the most optimistic prognostications for the Russian side, it would have taken years for them to take the Ukrainian fortress cities Kramatorsk and Sloviansk, if at all. This setback, however, not only wasted a tremendous amount of Russian resources and troops, but also pushed the target even further away. It marks now the official failure of Russian summer offensive.

items.title: The amount of Patriot interceptor missiles the US are using to counter Iranian attacks is mind-boggling. Between 60 and 100 missiles, possibly even more, fired in a matter of minutes, the majority being PAC-3 MSE interceptors. It is obvious that Iran is deliberately exhausting US stockpiles using rather cheap missiles. The political backlash in the US is already huge, and any further uncoordinated escalation is primarily hurting the US and the West altogether. The Iranian regime has also nothing seriously to fear from the Trump administration, because of the wasted time in the beginning of the year. Only a full-scale invasion would change their calculus, but of course, there is virtually a zero chance that this is going to happen. Hence, they are feeling emboldened. The White House is even not capable to grasp or admit that Tehran is clearly coordinating with Russia. The coordination is certainly going beyond providing target coordinates of US troops. Not to mention the surging oil price which helps them both. The only good news is that Ukraine is depleting Russia, and by extension Iran. But Washington is clearly squandering that momentum. Without any serious grand strategy by the US administration, which would also consider the inclusion of allies and partners, this whole war is a blunder of epic proportions. It is only the latest example how important a clear strategy, solid alliances and trust are.

items.title: Jared Kushner‘s Win-Win statement is exposing the absolute lack of understanding of the situation or worse. Putin is not thinking in „business terms“. He has accumulated wealth which he won’t be able to spend in 100 lifetimes, by some accounts making him even the richest person on earth. Putin is passed that. For him it is now only about legacy. He wants that people in the next centuries look back and call his name next to Peter the Great and Stalin. He will not achieve that by calling his invasion off. In the contrary, calling it off would only make him hang naked upside down the Kremlin wall, because he has achieved nothing other than diminishing Russia. Kushner‘s apparent ignorance not only shows why every peace offers fail, it also explains why it only fuels the war. Putin thinks for good reasons that he is dealing with absolute amateurs in the White House, who can get played with „business talk“, giving him only more time. Just look the last two years and you see that Russia hasn’t moved an inch, and under Putin never ever will. Any half-intelligent person would question the cause of actions and alter the direction. But those in the White House can help themselves. This whole stunt was predictably a waste of time.
